title: Budget and Revenue
text:
Figure 1 shows the relationship between movie budgets and the revenue made.

# generate the dataset 
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

df = pd.read_csv("films.csv")

plt.scatter(df["budget_musd"],df["revenue_musd"])
plt.xlabel("Budget in MUSD")
plt.ylabel("Revenue in MUSD")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Movie budget versus revenue. There is a positive association.

title: Runtime and Ratings
text:
Figure 1 shows relationship between movie runtime in minutes and the IMDB rating.

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")

plt.scatter(films["runtime_min"],films["imdb_rating"])
plt.xlabel("Runtime (minutes)")
plt.ylabel("IMDB Rating")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Movie runtime in minutes versus IMDB rating. This association is more nuanced and random-looking.

title: The Bond Films!
text:
This page foucses on the box-office revenue for the James Bond Films over time.

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")

bond = films[films["franchise"] == "James Bond"]
bond = bond.sort_values("year")

plt.plot(bond["year"], bond["revenue_musd"], marker="o")
plt.xlabel("Year")
plt.ylabel("Revenue in MUSD")
plt.show()







Figure 1: James Bond film revenues over time.





The first James Bond film in this dataset was released in 1995, and the last was released in 2021
